newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary overnight rate slides in slow market.
newsitem.headline: Hungary overnight rate slides in slow market.

text.p: Hungarian overnight rates eased in relatively low turnover on Thursday because banks had built up enough liquidity not to need to borrow, dealers said.
"The market is calm and well-balanced," said Erika Kaiser of Budapest Bank.
The overnight rate ended the day at 21.375 percent after hovering between 21.375 and 21.75 percent during trading. The rate closed Wednesday at 21.875 percent.
Although tomorrow is the last day of the current reserve period, banks do not need to borrow as their reserves are ample, Kaiser said.
"Over the last few weeks, everybody has been carefully managing their reserves to avoid the kind of sharp rises that took place at the end of the last period (two weeks ago)," she said.
In the middle of January, overnight rates rose to above 27 percent for a few days.
A large inflow of funds to banks from reverse repos that matured recently also helped stem the bank's appetite for forints, said Adam Szilagyi of ABM-AMRO.
